3477ec4c7ae07150.description: ## About Alpha Nodus Alpha Nodus builds Gravity, an AI-powered operations platform for outpatient diagnostic imaging centers and radiology practices in the U.S. Gravity takes on work that imaging centers still do by hand: reading faxed orders, checking insurance, getting prior authorizations, scheduling patients and chasing payment. Each of these is a product line with its own customers, payers, workflows and problems. ## The role You'll own the health of one Gravity product line at a time, starting with prior authorization. You'll learn how that work really happens at our customers, find where it breaks and why, turn what you find into a short, ranked list of what our team should do next, and keep track of whether it worked. The job is part business analyst, part product analyst. You'll spend as much time with customers' staff, support tickets and real cases as you do in SQL. Your output isn't a dashboard. It's decisions and action items that make a product line work better for the imaging centers that use it. ## What you'll do ### Go deep on a product line (about 40%) * Learn the workflow end to end: how an imaging center gets a prior authorization today, payer by payer, from the order arriving to approval or denial. * Read real cases, sit in on customer calls and talk to the people doing the work, so you understand the problem before you open a chart. * Find where work stalls and why: payer rules, missing clinical information, referring-office habits, gaps in our product, or how a customer uses it. * Size every problem in numbers: how often it happens, how much time it costs, and what it means for the center's revenue and its patients. ### Turn findings into action (about 30%) * Turn what you find into clear, ranked action items. Each has an owner (product, engineering, customer success or the customer), the evidence behind it, and the number that will tell us it worked. * Write requirements engineering can build from: the problem, the evidence, the user story, acceptance criteria and edge cases. * Follow through. Check in with owners, push for decisions, and close the loop when a fix ships. * Bring short, decision-ready findings to customer reviews and product planning. ### Keep a tab on performance (about 20%) * Define the metrics that show whether a product line is working, such as turnaround time, first-pass approval rate, denial rate by payer, automation rate, staff touches per case and customer adoption. Write them down so everyone reads them the same way. * Review them every week, catch drops early, and explain what changed before anyone has to ask. * Report each product line's health to the founder and the team, along with what you're doing about it. ### Help our AI get better (about 10%) * Gravity's AI agents do much of this work. Because you'll know what the right outcome looks like, you'll build and refresh the test sets we use to evaluate them: real cases labeled with the correct outcome, covering the payers and edge cases that matter. * Review where the agents go wrong with engineering, and feed those cases back into your action list. ## What you'll bring * 4–7 years as a business analyst, product analyst or operations analyst, ideally including time at a product company or startup. * A track record of going into a messy process or product area, finding what's really going wrong, and getting a team to fix it. You can tell us the before and after in numbers. * Strong SQL and spreadsheet skills. You pull and check your own numbers rather than waiting for someone else to. * Experience with a BI tool such as QuickSight, Metabase, Power BI or Tableau. * Experience mapping processes and writing requirements or user stories. * A habit of reading raw cases and talking to the people doing the work before trusting a dashboard. * Clear writing: a one-page finding for a customer, and an action list a team can execute. * Comfort influencing people you don't manage, and pushing back with evidence. * Willingness to work U.S. business hours with U.S. customers. ## Nice to have * U.S. healthcare operations experience: prior authorization, eligibility, revenue cycle, payer policies or denials management. * Experience in radiology, imaging or another operations-heavy healthcare setting. * Product analytics tools such as Mixpanel, Amplitude or PostHog, and basic Python for analysis. * Labeling data or reviewing outputs from AI or LLM-based products. * Working with HIPAA-regulated data. ## What this role is not This isn't a data engineering or machine learning role. You won't build data pipelines, run a warehouse or train models; our engineering team owns that. If your best work is building ETL or data platforms, this probably isn't the right fit, and we'd rather say so up front. ## Why this role You'll own outcomes, not reports. A product line's performance is yours to understand and improve. Your action items go straight to the team that builds the product, and you'll see them ship. You'll see how AI agents are built, measured and improved in production, and you'll help decide what "correct" means. You'll work closely with the founder and with U.S. imaging centers, in a field where getting this right means patients get scanned sooner. * Location: Bangalore office, working U.S. hours * Reports to: Founder / Head of Product * Experience: 4–7 years
